blocks.text: CEBU CITY, Philippines — Students in several Metro Cebu cities and municipalities will shift to alternative learning arrangements on Wednesday, October 14, as authorities respond to air quality levels classified as “very unhealthy” that could pose health risks to students, teachers, and school personnel. As of 9 p.m. Tuesday, Cebu City, Mandaue City, Talisay City, and Minglanilla announced the suspension of face-to-face classes, following air quality monitoring reports from the Department of Environment and Natural Resources-Environmental Management Bureau in Central Visayas (DENR-EMB-7). ‘Very unhealthy’ air quality The Metro Cebu monitoring station recorded an Air Quality Index (AQI) of 164 at 6 […]...
